plan: [I will bid my true value of $47. In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever the second-highest bid is below your value and pay that price, avoiding overpaying. With independent values and rational opponents, shading cannot increase expected profit. This maximizes expected (long-run) earnings.]

[In a sealed-bid second-price auction, bidding my true private value is a weakly dominant strategy: I win when my value exceeds competitors' bids and pay the second-highest bid, so shading can't increase expected payoff. No history to exploit and values are independent. Therefore bid my true value to maximize expected profit.]

[I will bid my true private value of $36. In a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest wins, pays the second-highest), bidding your true value is a dominant strategy with independent private values. Andy and Betty, being rational, will likely bid their values as well. Bidding 36 maximizes expected profit and avoids overpaying.]
